newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-NZ GAINS EARLY WICKET VS ENGLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-NZ GAINS EARLY WICKET VS ENGLAND.

text.p: New Zealand snapped up an early England wicket to have the tourists 39 for one at tea on the second day of the first cricket test on Saturday.
Opener Nick Knight was leg before wicket to fast-medium bowler Simon Doull after labouring 28 balls over five runs.
At the interval, captain Mike Atherton had reached 18 and Alec Stewart, having faced only nine balls, was on 13.
Atherton had struck four boundaries as he bids to get himself back into form.
He hooked Danny Morrison to the fine leg boundary, drove Doull through the covers and steered him to third man, and despatched Chris Cairns through mid wicket.
Stewart hooked a short ball from Cairns into the stand at backward square leg, then cut the last ball of the session to the point fence.
Earlier, New Zealand's first innings ended soon after the drinks break in the second session at 390.
The last man out was century-maker Stephen Fleming, who fell to a smart, low catch by Dominic Cork off his own bowling for 129.
It was Fleming's first test hundred. He notched it up in 369 minutes from 254 balls and hit 18 fours and one six.
New Zealand suffered a setback in their bid to pass 400 when fast-medium Darren Gough picked up three wickets in the space of 12 balls.
He had captain Lee Germon caught behind attempting a hook and Dipak Patel leg before wicket first ball before getting Doull caught at second slip.
Gough finished with four for 91 off 32 overs while Cork took three for 96 from 32.5 overs.
